title: Man shot during 2024 Trump campaign rally in Butler dies
description: In a post on his social media site Truth Social, Trump called Copenhaver a "true American patriot". "More than two years ago in Butler, Pennsylvania,
body: In a post on his social media site Truth Social, Trump called Copenhaver a "true American patriot". "More than two years ago in Butler, Pennsylvania, a crazed gunman attempted to stifle our America First Movement. Instead, Jim and so many other wonderful Patriots who love our Country, stood united in defense of our shared values of Freedom, Liberty, and Justice," Trump said. "Our hearts and prayers are with the Copenhaver family, especially his incredible wife Marianne."An attorney for Copenhaver's family said his dedication to the US was a "defining part of his life". "As a veteran, he proudly served our nation in the armed forces, and his love of country never wavered," the lawyer said in a statement to the BBC's US partner CBS News. In an interview with CBS a year after the Butler rally, Copenhaver and David Dutch, the third attendee who was shot, said they had been through infections and surgeries after being wounded. Copenhaver was shot in the arm and the abdomen. A year later, the bullet was still lodged in his body next to his spine, he told CBS, causing him to walk with a cane. Both Dutch and Copenhaver sued the federal government for damages in June, arguing the Secret Service failed to ensure their safety and was therefore liable for their injuries. Republicans in the US House of Representatives also paid tribute to Copenhaver on Friday, saying in a social media post: "Jim endured unimaginable hardship with strength and perseverance."

title: Ed Sheeran concerts cancelled becuase of bad weather
description: Ed Sheeran's concerts in Massachusetts on Friday and Saturday have been cancelled because of severe weather warnings in the area.The singer had been s
body: Ed Sheeran's concerts in Massachusetts on Friday and Saturday have been cancelled because of severe weather warnings in the area.The singer had been scheduled to perform two shows at the Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, near Boston, as part of his current US tour.The tour has been in the headlines because of a row over a decision to drop Sheeran's support act Macklemore for making pro-Palestinian comments on stage. Stadium owners including the Gillette Stadium's Robert Kraft lobbied for his removal.A statement from the venue, external said: "Due to the severe weather warnings in place in Boston and across New England throughout the weekend and following consultation with local officials, the promoter and tour have made the difficult decision to cancel the Ed Sheeran concerts at Gillette Stadium."It added: "The decision was made with the safety of fans, staff and everyone involved in the shows as the top priority."Refunds are available now at the point of purchase. Ticketholders who purchased through Ticketmaster will be automatically refunded."Weather warnings for high winds are in force in the area until the early hours of Sunday, and officials have told drivers to minimise travel.Sheeran was at the eye of a very different storm last week after the decision to drop Macklemore from his tour.The decision came after the rapper made on-stage comments at earlier concerts including calling for "free Palestine" and referring to "genocide" in Gaza, as well as showing images of Gaza.Kraft, who is Jewish, accused the US rapper of hate speech and said Macklemore would not be allowed to appear at the Gillette Stadium, the home of his New England Patriots American football team.Sheeran said the decision to drop Macklemore was made by his promoter, not by him. The promoter said venue owners including Kraft would have refused to let the concerts take place if Macklemore was on the bill.Macklemore's removal from the tour led Sheeran's other support and backing artists to pull out in protest, and sparked a heated debate over free speech and the role of politics in music.Returning to the stage last weekend, Sheeran told fans he "had to take and make difficult decisions - and I am making mistakes - and I'm so, so sorry".

schema.headline: Ed Sheeran concerts cancelled becuase of bad weather

title: Some BBC channels and radio stations 'may well' have to close, director general says
description: Brittin took over as BBC director general in May after a decade as president of Google in Europe, the Middle East and Africa.Asked by Kuenssberg if he
body: Brittin took over as BBC director general in May after a decade as president of Google in Europe, the Middle East and Africa.Asked by Kuenssberg if he would allow a programme to be made and presented by AI, Brittin replied: "I would do, within guardrails."He added: "We want to experiment with this technology and understand what it can and can't do, but I'm here because I believe in human creativity."I don't think anything we do should be replaced by AI. I think there are lots of places where AI can help us make the licence fee go further, but also help us in our decision-making and creativity. But it's not a substitute for humans."He also warned of the danger of a handful of tech companies having too much control over information in the future."We're also in this moment where AI is in takeoff. So I think there's a danger that six companies will control access to information in future and the creation of information and misinformation," he said."Six companies, none of them European, let alone British. In that world, here's the BBC. It's the most trusted organisation by over half a billion people."Asked if he trusted big tech companies he replied: "There's a lot of platforms out there, so I wouldn't trust any platform innately."And I think what you do is you keep under review how those things work and whether your content can show up in the right place and fulfil its mission."I think the BBC and our apps and services should be the antidote to the algorithm. Everywhere else you go is driven by some commercial interest."The interview will be available on BBC Sounds and YouTube on Saturday 26 September, then on Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg on BBC One and iPlayer at 09:00 BST on 27 September.

schema.headline: Some BBC channels and radio stations 'may well' have to close, director general says

title: FA Cup Final assistant referee says tumours have ended his career
description: It was May 2025 and life was good for Premier League and Fifa assistant referee Dan Robathan.In fact, he was flying high.Years of climbing the footbal
body: It was May 2025 and life was good for Premier League and Fifa assistant referee Dan Robathan.In fact, he was flying high.Years of climbing the football ladder had paid off and he was running the line at the FA Cup final between Crystal Palace and Manchester City.But just months after this career highlight, symptoms Dan thought were sciatic nerve pain and wear and tear were revealed to be benign tumours in his spine, which needed to be operated on immediately."I saw a neurosurgeon who told me I had two tumours, initially I thought it was one, but it was two," Dan tells BBC Newsbeat."It was compressing nerves, there was a chance it could affect a motor nerve which means it could affect function in my leg."I needed to go home, lay down and not move. I did that for 15 days, my life turned upside down overnight."BBC Newsbeat met Dan at a football pitch in Norwich, close to where he lives, where he revealed the struggles he has had in trying to regain his fitness and mobility. Dan picked up his first flag at 10 years old, working his way up from grassroots football to the lines at more than 200 Premier League clashes and World Cup qualifiers. Speaking at the time of the FA Cup final, Dan said it was "a privilege to stand there on behalf of over 37,000 referees across the country". The chances of becoming an elite level referee are low. The FA describes Fifa match officials, external as the "pinnacle of the officiating ladder".Photos of Dan over the last few years show him doing everything from embracing then Liverpool manager Arne Slot to explaining a decision to Emiliano Martinez, and officiating games without fans due to the Covid pandemic.And in his social media posts, Dan gives a glimpse of everything you would expect from an official at elite level - from the roar of fans to sprinting to be in the right place during split second decisions.To the outside world, all looked well."I started having quite bad problems with sexual dysfunction or bladder issues where I'd have to sit down to urinate and I couldn't stand up," he explains."It got to a point in September [2025] where something's not right at all." A neurosurgeon confirmed to Dan he had two tumours in his spine – and his life ground to a halt."It was fear, anxiety, not knowing how long it will take me to get back."What would my life look like? Will I be a normal man? Will I walk again?"Surgeons removed one tumour and left one alone, which was deemed safe.The 38-year-old says he still has days where he struggles to walk, or where his back feels "on fire"."My body just can't do what I want it to do," he says.Dan underwent testing to confirm his tumours weren't linked to genetics, which was reassuring, but still leaves him facing the unknown."It's a loss of identity. I've been 'Dan the ref' since I was 10 years old. "It's 28 years of being who I am, it's my personality."When you have the recognition that that sort of life is over, psychologically it is really tough." Dan is now working with a psychologist to decide the path forward. "I feel like a 16-year-old who's just left school and trying to work out what I want to do with my life," he jokes. "I have a few options, staying in football."[But] I don't know if I will be able to with the mental health problems I've had."Can I stay involved in a sport that I loved but can't do myself?"One thing he is certain of, is going into the future with his family."I want to put my son, fiancée, my stepchildren first. I want to try and advocate for men's mental health, for men speaking about health issues. "If I can help one or two men in the process, I've done my job."And Dan accepts that if he gets back into football it would need to be for the right reasons. "I need to get that fire my belly."

schema.headline: FA Cup Final assistant referee says tumours have ended his career

title: Jay-Z rape accuser formally withdraws allegation
description: A woman who accused Jay-Z of raping her when she was 13 has formally said her allegation was untrue.The unnamed woman filed a lawsuit in 2024 claiming
body: A woman who accused Jay-Z of raping her when she was 13 has formally said her allegation was untrue.The unnamed woman filed a lawsuit in 2024 claiming she had been drugged and raped by Jay-Z, real name Shawn Carter, and Sean "Diddy" Combs at a party after the MTV Video Music Awards in 2000.The stars denied the allegation and she dropped the lawsuit last year. Carter then sued her and her lawyers.In a statement filed in that case on Thursday, she wrote: "Shawn 'Jay-Z' Carter never raped me. I have never met or spoken to Mr. Carter. Mr. Carter never engaged in any inappropriate conduct toward me whatsoever."The woman, known in court documents by the pseudonym Jane Doe, also said: "My claims that Mr Carter and Mr Combs raped me while a third celebrity, [name redacted] watched are false. There is no truth to any of my claims against Mr Carter."I understand my false accusations have caused Mr Carter immense pain, suffering, and damage that can never be fully undone."Carter had vehemently denied the accusations, saying they were a "blackmail attempt" and describing them as "frivolous, fictitious and appalling allegations".When the accuser dropped her case in February 2025, the rapper, who is married to singer Beyoncé, said: "The trauma that my wife, my children, loved ones and I have endured can never be dismissed."The woman, from Alabama, has now been removed from Carter's lawsuit. She said she had not received any money from the rap superstar or anyone acting on his behalf, and had not been paid to make her latest declaration.The rapper is still suing the woman's former lawyers, led by Tony Buzbee.In a statement to Rolling Stone, external, which first reported Jane Doe's new declaration, Buzbee said he had not seen it.He said: "We have multiple lawyers (at least four) who dealt with Ms Doe long before she met me. She gave the exact same story to each. If for some reason now she is claiming she lied to us and the court, that's new information."When Carter filed his lawsuit against the woman and her lawyers in February 2025, Buzbee claimed at the time that Carter's investigators had "repeatedly harassed, threatened and harangued this poor woman for weeks, trying to intimidate her and make her recant her story".In her new declaration, the woman said: "I never received any threat from Mr Carter or anyone acting on his behalf."Setting out the events that led to her allegation, the woman said she saw an advert on Facebook in September or October 2024 looking for people who might have sexual assault claims against Combs. "The ad triggered memories of being raped when I was 13 years old," she said.She was contacted by a law firm but was not provided with a draft of the lawsuit containing her allegations and did not authorise it before it was filed in October 2024, she said.She also said Buzbee and other lawyers acting on her behalf filed it "without conducting any independent investigation, background inquiry, or due diligence, and without obtaining any corroboration of the allegations".She said: "The October Complaint alleges that Mr Carter and Mr Combs raped me when I was a minor while an unnamed celebrity watched. As discussed above, these allegations were false."Buzbee also represents numerous other people who have made allegations against Combs. Combs denied Jane Doe's claims, which his lawyer described at the time as one of a number of civil cases "pushed forward by an attorney more focused on media headlines than legal merit".The BBC has contacted Buzbee for comment.In July 2025, Combs was convicted by a criminal court on prostitution-related charges involving his two ex-girlfriends, and is currently serving a four-year prison sentence.

schema.headline: Jay-Z rape accuser formally withdraws allegation

title: Cole Palmer misses too many opportunities to play for England - Thomas Tuchel
description: Cole Palmer "misses too many opportunities" to play for England after the Chelsea forward pulled out of the latest squad, says manager Thomas Tuchel.T
body: Cole Palmer "misses too many opportunities" to play for England after the Chelsea forward pulled out of the latest squad, says manager Thomas Tuchel.The withdrawal of Palmer came as a surprise as he has started all five of Chelsea's matches in the Premier League so far this season, though Tuchel says he had been playing with "discomfort and pain".The 24-year-old was left out of the World Cup squad by Tuchel and has featured just three times since the German took charge of the Three Lions in January 2025. "My understanding is that he is playing with discomfort and pain, and he cannot compete at the highest level with discomfort and pain. So he withdrew and informed us, and Chelsea informed us." Tuchel said."For sure. It is a missed opportunity. He misses too many opportunities. I don't blame him for it. It is just a fact."He misses way too many camps with injuries, and I only want to rely on what I witness and see within in my team, and for that you have to be in camp."And if you're not in camp, there is a next level to impress that you cannot achieve because you can only do it when you are actually on the pitch with me. So yes, it is a missed opportunity."It is understood Palmer is currently abroad completing an injury-specific training plan.Chelsea's non international players have been given days off and have been permitted to travel if they so wish.Palmer has been accompanied by a Chelsea rehabilitation coach on his overseas trip.Declan Rice, Tino Livramento, Marcus Rashford and Kobbie Mainoo are the other players who pulled out with injury. Tuchel said he was not worried that players may put their clubs above playing for their country. "We are not managing load. When I was in club football, I used the term 'international break' and, when you hear it from the other side, it is a totally different picture," he said."It is a competitive environment, but it is also an environment that the players love to be a part of. "That is what togetherness and brotherhood look like, and that is what we have created since last September in qualifying. We will never compromise on that."We will never let it creep in that we have a feeling players do not want to come. We focus on the guys who absolutely want to play for England."The match against world champions Spain at Wembley on Saturday is England's first game since the end of the World Cup. The Three Lions ended the tournament with a 6-4 win in the Bronze medal match against France, but were criticised for the way they lost 2-1 to Argentina in the semi-final. England led 1-0 going into the final 15 minutes but dropped deep and conceded possession, with Argentina scoring two goals in the final minutes to reach the final.Tuchel does not think there will be a negative reaction from the fans because of the result."I would be very surprised if the atmosphere would hold a third place or an accident in the 85th minute of a semi-final against us and against our team, that would surprise me a lot." Tuchel said. "The time and how and how fast it sold out shows me how excited everyone is to come and watch. "That's the reality of it, Spain make it hard for you to play a high intensity game. They are happy to control the ball and the rhythm. "There can be spells when we will suffer and have to suffer, but there can be spells where we dominate and can bring the attributes that make us strong, so let's see how it plays out."

schema.headline: Cole Palmer misses too many opportunities to play for England - Thomas Tuchel

title: PM says bailed sex offender case must be reviewed
description: The prime minister has said that the decision to bail a sex offender and repeatedly allow him to return to his home overlooking the playground he targ
body: The prime minister has said that the decision to bail a sex offender and repeatedly allow him to return to his home overlooking the playground he targeted must be reviewed. Zafer Dogan, 32, of Enfield, north London, was jailed on Thursday for two years and four months for taking thousands of pictures of children and using AI software to "nudify" them.Andy Burnham called the case "disturbing", adding: "I would ask those working across the criminal justice system to look at it and to make any necessary changes as a result."The Ministry of Justice said while the Crown Prosecution Service had the right to challenge them, final bail decisions were "made by the independent judiciary".The ministry added: "The protection of victims, witnesses, and the public must always be considered when deciding whether or not an offender should be released on bail."London's victims' commissioner Andrea Simon said victims and their families had been "grossly failed" by the court system that granted Dogan bail.She said the case showed "the justice system did not centre victims" and called for a multi-agency review.Speaking outside the court where Dogan was jailed, Met Police Commissioner Sir Mark Rowley criticised the "unfathomable decisions" of the justice system.Burnham told BBC London's political editor Karl Mercer that Sir Mark "certainly has a point and it needs to be heard"."It's a matter for the courts when these decisions are made," the prime minister said. "They need to hear the voice of the commissioner of the Metropolitan Police."This case is disturbing and I would ask those working across the criminal justice system to look at it and make any necessary changes as a result."Burnham also told BBC London the plan to release some offenders before the end of their custodial sentences, to free up space in prisons, was "not an ideal situation"."The failure to build prison spaces over a number of years has led to this unacceptable situation," he said.Dogan had pleaded guilty to three counts of making indecent images of a child, which included 900 category C images, 294 category B images and 653 category A images, which are the most serious.He also admitted possessing extreme pornography, possessing a prohibited image of a child, creating purported intimate images of an adult, obstructing a constable in the execution of their duty and a further two counts of making indecent photographs of a child.According to the police, he had taken more than 5,000 pictures, many from his bedroom window.Despite protests from the police and prosecutors, he had previously been bailed back to his flat, forcing one family who had fallen victim to his crimes to move into temporary accommodation.Speaking on BBC Radio 4's Today, Simon said: "I think victims and their families were grossly failed by the decision to allow this paedophile to return to an address where he was overlooking a playground near to his victims."The case [shows that] the justice system just does not centre victims. To know that the police and prosecutors opposed bail multiple times, but nevertheless, he was returned to the community, is an indication that the capacity pressures on prisons are not being balanced with the impacts that that's having on victims' lives."We seem to be lurching from one crisis to another, and victim safety and their rights seem to be put to one side, as the justice system struggles."Simon's criticism was echoed by Sir Mark, who said: "Prosecutors rightly opposed bail on multiple occasions, building on officers' clear assessments of the great risk he posed, and yet bail decisions were ultimately made that prioritised the offender's interests over the safety and the peace of mind of the victims."Former Tory justice secretary Sir Robert Buckland told the BBC's The World At One: "Until justice is given the same priority that we give to health and education, this problem will recur."Dangerous men should not be released on bail when they are clearly going to go on and commit further offences."Sir Tom Winsor, former Her Majesty's Chief Inspector of Constabulary, told the programme: "Judges appear to be taking prison capacity into account."The result is prolific offenders are being bailed. Releasing dangerous people into the community is an extremely serious thing."Of course we have an independent judiciary but their obligation is to also explain their decisions."Simon said there were parallels to be drawn with the case of serial sex offender and murderer Simon Levy.Levy killed two women and raped a third in 2025 while on bail for other offences, after a series of decisions by authorities that left him free to roam the streets. Levy had been reported to the Metropolitan Police for a sexual assault in 2017. He then assaulted two women in 2018, but was only convicted for those offences in 2021.After being released from prison - where he sexually assaulted a female officer - he committed other assaults before the 2025 murders.He was sentenced to life in prison in August.Sir Mark previously described that case as a "whole system failing", criticising the decision of the courts and Crown Prosecution Service to bail Levy, while also apologising for the Met's own failings in the case.Levy is a registered sex offender and was being monitored by police at the time of the attacks. The force failed to treat the first murder as such until after the second murder and released Levy on bail leaving him free to kill. It also failed to fully pursue a rape investigation and closed the case, meaning Levy went on to kill Sheryl Wilkins in the same place where he had attacked the surviving rape victim.Two Met police officers are currently under investigation by the police watchdog for downgrading Levy's risk to women - a decision that was not reversed even after police knew he was attacking women again.London's victims' commissioner Simon also raised concerns over the government's early release scheme which is set to see about 2,550 eligible offenders leaving jails in England and Wales by the end of the year."I hear from victims about what they think they want to do ahead of offenders' early releases from prison," she said. "They feel they may have to install security cameras or change their daily routines, or live in fear."Listen to the best of BBC Radio London on Sounds and follow BBC London on Facebook, external, X, external and Instagram, external. Send your story ideas to hello.bbclondon@bbc.co.uk, external

title: 'We're all broke': Would you chase a friend for £5?
description: Figure caption, Watch: We ask New Yorkers to share the smallest amount they'd ask a friend to pay backByYasmin RufoBusiness reporter Reporting fromNew
body: Figure caption, Watch: We ask New Yorkers to share the smallest amount they'd ask a friend to pay backByYasmin RufoBusiness reporter Reporting fromNew YorkYou pick up the bill for dinner, pay for the taxi home or grab a friend's coffee with the promise they'll pay you back later, but days go by and the money never arrives.At what point do you ask them for it again and how small is too small to chase?For some, $5 (£3.70) is worth a reminder, while for others, asking a friend to repay anything under $20 (£15) feels more awkward than simply taking the hit.Henry Payne says he's "sent a request for $8.50, but I wouldn't go lower than $8". The 21-year-old New Yorker adds that he will chase someone once but "two requests is insane"."I would rather swallow the $8.50 than send another request."He does admit that he's sometimes the person on the other side of the transaction and can be forgetful himself."For everyone that I haven't sent back money to, I just forgot, feel free to double request me."Image caption, Nouria (left) and Kaz are two students in New York who say money conversations with friends can be very awkward Kaz Jahanbini, 19, says needing to ask to be paid back in the first place can be frustrating."If someone bought me something, I'm immediately paying them back. So then I'm thinking for them, what's the delay?"His rule for navigating friendship and finances is to "keep your wallet close but your friends closer".His friend Nouria agrees and says as a student "every extra dollar counts" but she would usually only ask for money back from a friend if it was more than $10.A recent study, external found that 76% of Gen Z who have fronted money for a group expense, like a trip or event, say they were not fully repaid, and 55% say it created tension or negatively affected a relationship. Image caption, Betsie believes there's a cultural difference between Brits and Americans For British student Betsie Brooke-Taylor, 19, the threshold to ask for money back is a fiver as she says "every little helps".She sees a cultural difference between the UK and US and even though "we are all broke, I think Americans are a bit more generous".Betsie also thinks technology makes settling small debts easier in the US, where payment apps such as Venmo are widely used.Venmo lets users send and request money through an app which includes the function of sending a reminder if someone hasn't paid you. In the US, more than 95 million people have a Venmo account, external."In the UK you have to ask for the account number and sort code, and not everyone has that on hand," she says.Image caption, Annika (left) and Hanako feel very differently about confronting a friend who hasn't paid them backFor 19-year-old Annika Violet, the amount she would ask back from a friend depends on whether she's consistently paying for them. "I prefer to do something where I get them this time and they get me next time but if I'm consistently paying and you're not, then I will request the $5."Unlike many, Annika doesn't find money conversations uncomfortable."I am so confrontational, I do not find it awkward. If you're my friend, you would pay me back."Annika's friend Hanako Stepper says she finds it awkward asking for money but wishes she didn't. "I've never chased anyone - I'm just sad if I don't get paid back."Annika's advice to those who do struggle to ask is to "be brave and bold"."If they are going to give you flak about it, maybe it's a sign they are not a good friend."How do you ask for money back without making it awkward?Money expert Laura Pomfret says many people feel embarrassed about asking to be paid back, and Britons in particular can find it awkward."We're often very British about asking for money back," she says, suggesting people may be worried about being judged as a "cheapskate".Her top tips for asking friends to pay up are: She adds that you shouldn't convince yourself that a debt is too small to justify asking for it as "if you want the money paid back then the amount shouldn't matter". And if the same friend repeatedly fails to pay, Pomfret suggests remembering it the next time you're about to pay for them and think twice. Image caption, Ella (left) and Katrina have a few friends who rarely pay them backSeveral people the BBC spoke to said the amount itself mattered less when somebody repeatedly failed to pay.New York student Ella Feuille, 21, says $15 is roughly the point at which she would consider requesting money.If a significant amount was owed, Ella says she would ask around three times before giving up but wouldn't necessarily forget about it."I have friends who I know now it has to go on their card because they're not going to pay me back."Her friend Katrina Dimingot agrees and says she much prefers a method where "we don't pay each other back, we just take it in turns to get things for each other". title: Daniel Thomas pleads not guilty after dinghy slashed in Channel
description: Image source, Elizabeth Cook/PA WireImage caption, Daniel Thomas was seen dabbing his eyes with a tissue at one point during the hearingBySteve Humphr
body: Image source, Elizabeth Cook/PA WireImage caption, Daniel Thomas was seen dabbing his eyes with a tissue at one point during the hearingBySteve HumphreyReporting fromBasingstoke Magistrates' CourtUpdated 1 hour agoAnti-migrant activist Daniel Thomas has pleaded not guilty to criminal damage after a video appeared to show him slashing at a dinghy in the Channel with a knife.The 37-year-old, known to his supporters as Danny Tommo, was arrested after the livestreamed video on Tuesday.Thomas, who appeared at Basingstoke Magistrates' Court in Hampshire via videolink, is also charged with failing to disclose the PIN to his phone.He pleaded not guilty to both charges and was remanded in custody until his next court appearance at Portsmouth Crown Court on 29 September.Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Daniel Thomas, known to his supporters as Danny Tommo, appeared in court via videolink (file photo)The court heard a crew member was on the boat while it was heard leaking air.Prosecutor Kevin Lucie told the court that Thomas, who was seen dabbing his eyes with a tissue at one point during the hearing, slashed an adrift boat with a knife and said: "You are on English territory. This is England. This is not France any more."Deputy Chief Magistrate Tan Ikram said the case could have been heard in the magistrates' court but Mr Thomas elected to be tried at crown court.Figure caption, Police had been examining livestream footage appearing to show Daniel Thomas slashing at a migrant boatFar-right activist Stephen Yaxley-Lennon, also known as Tommy Robinson, was among those in the public gallery.Some supporters also gathered outside the court.Posting on social media after the hearing, Yaxley-Lennon said: "Danny is being remanded to prison."His legal team will now prepare to fight at the crown court for his bail."Image source, PAImage caption, Police were positioned outside the courtHampshire police previously said an arrest had been made after a "boat that had an emergency responder on board" was damaged in the Channel on Tuesday.Several hundred people gathered outside a police investigation centre in Basingstoke on Thursday evening, believing that Thomas was inside.The demonstration, which seemed to pass off peacefully, began shortly before 18:30 BST. Protesters stood on the road outside the building and could be heard chanting "free DT".The crowd began to disperse at about 21:45 after they learned of the charges against Thomas.Get in touchYour Voice

title: Azerbaijan Grand Prix: Russell takes pole as Antonelli out after hitting wall
description: George Russell took an imperious pole position for Mercedes at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix as his team-mate and championship leader Kimi Antonelli crash
body: George Russell took an imperious pole position for Mercedes at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix as his team-mate and championship leader Kimi Antonelli crashed out.Russell beat Ferrari's Charles Leclerc by a massive 0.837 seconds while Antonelli, who leads the Britain by 81 points in the championship, will start in 16th.The Italian hit the inside wall at Turn One in the first session and was knocked out.McLaren's Oscar Piastri was third ahead of Red Bull's Isack Hadjar and McLaren's Lando Norris.Lewis Hamilton, compromised by running without a tow from another car, was sixth, ahead of the Alpine of Pierre Gasly and Red Bull's Max Verstappen.With a tow or slipstream worth as much as 0.5 seconds, Verstappen was following Norris on their final laps when the Briton made a mistake and went off track.That scuppered Verstappen's chances of competing closer to the front.But although the four-time champion said he believed he could have been on the front row, he acknolweged that he could not have beaten Russell.On a weekend in which Antonelli's running has been compromised by reliability problems that meant he missed out on half the possible running on Thursday, Russell absolutely delivered on Mercedes' dominant position on this unique track.Russell has looked comfortable all weekend and never looked in danger of being beaten for pole, his first since the Austrian Grand Prix at the end of June."That's probably the biggest margin I've had in my whole career," Russell said. "The lap felt really sweet and the car has been feeling great all weekend."Leclerc was somewhat taken aback by Mercedes' superiority, saying that the position was what he expected but the gap most definitely was not.At the bottom of the top 10, there was finally some good news for Williams, for whom Carlos Sainz achieved the team's first top 10 qualifying performance of the year with ninth on the grid.However, the Spaniard was later penalised for failing to slow for yellow caution flags and was given a five-place penalty.Williams have introduced a new chassis this weekend which has brought them down to the weight limit for the first time this season, after being as much as 25kg over at the start of the year.Along with some additional developments, it appears to have produced a significant step forwards, although the caveat is that Baku is a track that suits the characteristics of the Williams car and does not expose its weaknesses.Team-mate Alex Albon did not manage to secure a tow in the second part of qualifying, and was "anyway struggling with straight-line speed all session", and was 13th, just under 0.4secs behind the Spaniard. Sainz's penalty will promote him a place on the grid.Antonelli's error came on his second lap of the first session.He turned into the first corner too early, and the left front wheel clouted the inside wall, breaking the suspension.He initially tried to get the car back to the pits but was told by engineer Peter Bonnington to park up."Let me try," Antonelli pleaded, before Bonnington told him that either the track rod or upright was broken and there was no way Mercedes could fix that in the time they had to turn the car around before the next session.Antonelli had been on the back foot all Friday trying to catch up time lost to a hydraulic problem that had stopped his car on track halfway through first practice, and was not repaired until halfway into the second.It was Antonelli's first major mistake of the season since he crashed heavily in final practice at the first race of the season in Australia.

schema.headline: Azerbaijan Grand Prix: Russell takes pole as Antonelli out after hitting wall

title: Kevin Pietersen: Former England batter on Harry Brook and working with Test side before Ashes
description: Kevin Pietersen is asked, after everything that came before, what he would have said if told he would work for the England and Wales Cricket board aga
body: Kevin Pietersen is asked, after everything that came before, what he would have said if told he would work for the England and Wales Cricket board again one day.In 2014, he was sacked by the ECB in one of most ugly and acrimonious periods in English cricketing history – a period that brought one of the most exciting but divisive international careers to an end."What do you think I'd have said," Pietersen says with a smile.Bigger stars in English cricket are harder to find.This is the man who had a brief but high-profile relationship with American celebrity Caprice, married a pop star, Jessica from Liberty X, and once tried to explain cricket to Taylor Swift on The Graham Norton Show.Back in the dressing room as a mentor, he is speaking to the media at Headingley - the location of his famous "it's tough being me" press conference.The hair is greyer, but he still carries all of that aura."I'm 46, man," he says, asked whether animosity remains."That stuff is so long gone. I am a completely different person."I live in South Africa. I love doing what I do. I am just here to help Brendon first and foremost, help the players try and become the best versions of themselves."Pietersen was the most intriguing of appointments to England's dressing room staff because of his own history, but also what he has said before.While commentating on England's white-ball tour of India last year, he suggested the Brendon McCullum outfit were not training enough."Clearly the perceptions I had before being asked to do the job were completely different to what I feel now," he says."It is nice to being part of an England team and set-up that is actually really, really driven."Pietersen answers every question with poise. Almost all are given and lengthy, considered responses.His only terse response comes when pushed on what exactly those preconceptions were - and how quickly they took to disappear."You know what the preconceptions were," he says. "I am not going near it."Despite that, he appears to be loving his return.Pietersen is "not sitting here wanting to be the coach of England" but wants to help McCullum and the players, many of whom grew up idolising him.One of those, Tom Banton, said last week he is still in awe of the four-time Ashes-winner, so much so he was struggling to build up the courage to speak to him."He wants a YouTube channel," Pietersen laughs. Pietersen, a 50-over great who played in a way ahead of his time, can also help him there.His official title is "specialist mentor" and he will dip in and out to work with the white-ball teams through to the 50-over World Cup next autumn.Before the first ODI in Durham, England posted a clip on social media of Pietersen leading a batting session.Holding court, he had Joe Root and Rehan Ahmed alike involved in a batting drill on how to rotate the strike against spin."All I want to be is a great person to these guys," Pietersen says."I want to be the best guy in the room, so that they come to me, and they ask me for information, and if I've got stuff for them, I'll give it to them."I am lucky to have worn every T-shirt an England cricketer can wear – the good, the bad the ugly."I can potentially help them to stay away from the ugly."Pietersen's eyes roll slightly when he is asked about Ben Stokes' recent comments comparing Harry Brook's talents to his.Pietersen, like Brook, was a maverick – a batter capable of incredible highs. Those highs mean the lows come with a disproportionate level of criticism."Where I can help him is playing situations, because there was a lot of method in my madness," Pietersen says."Yes, occasionally, I got out to reckless shots and crazy shots in the '80s and '90s but there was a lot of structure to the way that I batted."I've still got notes on my phone on how I played in T20 cricket, one-day cricket, Test match cricket, and about hitting straight back at the stumps, and the techniques, and how I did it, and don't play certain shots."That all-round structure is something I could potentially help him with because he's so flipping good."It's actually frightening how good he is and how good he can be."And Pietersen says he will not limit himself to working purely on white-ball cricket.He has already spoken to new Test coach Stephen Fleming about how he can help the Test batters during his time with the white-ball squads.Though he said he would not have time for a full-time role, he suggested he is open to working with the Test side before next summer's home Ashes series."I have got a pretty mad schedule," he says. "I wouldn't say no."I don't think that necessarily means I need to be in a dressing room."There is a lot of time in the lead up to an Ashes series and a tour of South Africa, when I will be with the Test batters. "There are conversations I can have there."Who knows how long this will last. England may as well make the most of this second chance.

schema.headline: Kevin Pietersen: Former England batter on Harry Brook and working with Test side before Ashes

title: Noah Woods died after leaving park through gap in fence, inquest hears
description: Suffolk Coroner's Court heard from police that Noah had left the playground,  walked into a memorial garden and left that through an open gate. He the
body: Suffolk Coroner's Court heard from police that Noah had left the playground,  walked into a memorial garden and left that through an open gate. He then ran down a path on a new housing estate towards nearby Decoy Pond.Det Ch Insp Matt Connick from Suffolk Police told the court that CCTV showed Noah in the play area being looked after by a relative, which was "part of a normal routine".The detective said Noah "left through a gap in the fence leading to the memorial garden where he left through an open gate".After he had left the play area, he was closely followed by the relative trying to catch up with him, Connick added.The inquest heard the relative had shouted out to Noah, who lived in neighbouring East Bergholt, but he went out of sight shortly afterwards.Another man was said to have joined the search and then police were called.At the time of the search, volunteers were told that Noah was non-verbal and partially deaf. A statement from Brantham Parish Council, which maintains the play area at Merriam Close, said it was "deeply saddened by Noah's death and our thoughts remain with his family and all those affected at this extremely difficult time"."The parish council understands that there was a break in the internal fencing, being constructed to separate the play area from the memorial garden, however the whole of the area at Merriam Close, including the play area and memorial garden are completely enclosed by appropriate perimeter fencing," it said."The council will co-operate fully with any investigation and, while inquiries are ongoing, does not consider it appropriate to comment further."The written tribute from Noah's family said he was at the centre of their world."He was part of a loving and caring family, living with his mummy, daddy and his little baby brother," it said."Every Tuesday since the day he was born Noah went to the park with a treasured relative. They had the most wonderful relationship, they loved playing chase together, running around, and exploring the play equipment. "Noah was being assessed for autism, although he had not received a diagnosis. He also had mild hearing loss and was speech delayed. "Despite the challenges he faced, he was learning every day. He was saying new words all the time and had only just started finding and using his little voice."Part of the tribute, from Noah's mother Charlie, said: "If there is one thing we could ask of people, it is to hold their children a little tighter, cherish every moment, and never take those precious memories for granted."You can read the full family tribute here:At least 1,300 people helped to try to find Noah in the following 24 hours.Helicopters, dog units and members of the public had been scouring the area, close to the River Stour on the Suffolk-Essex border.Divers from the Metropolitan Police went into Decoy Pond on 16 September in an area where Noah was last seen.His body was found five metres from the edge within submerged tree roots, at a depth of 1.8 metres.

schema.headline: Noah Woods died after leaving park through gap in fence, inquest hears

title: Sir David Beckham nets £38.5m after World Cup ad deals
description: Sir David Beckham has netted a £38.5m payout from his sports, fashion, and media business after the 2026 Men's Football World Cup helped it bring in r
body: Sir David Beckham has netted a £38.5m payout from his sports, fashion, and media business after the 2026 Men's Football World Cup helped it bring in record profits.The former England star's DRJB Holdings, which includes the Beckham brand, reported an almost £50m profit in 2025, a 46% jump compared to a year earlier. Sales rose from £72.2m to £84m.The rise was driven by a slew of advertising partnerships struck in the runup to the tournament, including with Bank of America, McDonald's, Verizon, and PepsiCo Lay's.Sir David, Britain's first billionaire sportsman, was commonly seen in adverts during the summer's World Cup.In the US, it was difficult for fans to watch a game without coming across Beckham in adverts for Stella Artois, Home Depot and Lay's crisps - known as Walkers in the UK.Sir David also launched menswear collections for Hugo Boss last year, as well as a pair of Adidas Predator football boots and an eyewear range with Italian glasses maker Safilo.Revenues at DRJB, of which Beckham owns almost half, were boosted by growth in Beckham's health supplements business too.DRJB paid its shareholders £38.9m, followed by a special £46.6m payment after the end of the financial year.Sir David's share of those dividends would have been around £38.5m due to how much of the company he owns.The remainder of DRJB is owned by New York-based Authentic Brands Group, which also owns Reebok, as well as the rights to other celebrity brands such as comedian and actor Kevin Hart.Authentic's entertainment chief executive Corey Salter said the performance showed Sir David's name is "one of the most powerful global brands in sport, lifestyle, entertainment and much more"."It's been an outstanding year, from new partnerships to important philanthropic campaigns and overall brand growth," he said.Sir David previously drew criticism for associating himself with a country where same-sex relationships are illegal by acting as an ambassador for the 2022 Men's Football World Cup in Qatar."It was an important competition and one I was proud to be part of," he said at the time, adding that he had engaged with the LGBTQ community during the tournament.

schema.headline: Sir David Beckham nets £38.5m after World Cup ad deals

title: British climber dies after falling 60m on Spanish mountainside
description: A 28-year-old British climber has died after falling about 60m (200ft) from one of the highest mountains in northern Spain. The man fell into a vertic
body: A 28-year-old British climber has died after falling about 60m (200ft) from one of the highest mountains in northern Spain. The man fell into a vertical gully while descending from the summit of Torrecerredo in the Cantabrian Mountains on Thursday, the Spanish Civil Guard said.Police and an air unit were deployed to the scene after emergency services were called at about 13:45 local time (11:45 GMT). The man's body and belongings were recovered by a mountain rescue unit. The UK Foreign Office said it was in contact with local authorities "following reports of the death of a British national in Spain".The Civil Guard said two mountain specialists were lowered by winch to the site of the accident, on the eastern face of the mountain.The identity of the climber, who Spanish authorities said was English, has not been given. The accident occurred when he was about 20 metres from the mountain's summit.His body has been transported to the Institute of Legal Medicine, which provides forensic pathology services, in Asturias, the Civil Guard said.Torrecerredo, which has an elevation of about 2,650m, is in the Picos de Europa, which is popular with climbers and walkers.Sepa Asturias - the body responsible for emergency services in the region - said it also transported a 54-year-old French woman to hospital after she suffered a leg injury on the mountain range on Thursday afternoon.

schema.headline: British climber dies after falling 60m on Spanish mountainside
